meta.purpose: DataCenter re-tag, 16 October 2026, under the loosened ruling 1: DataCenter = yes when a validated ref names the pipeline and mentions data centers at all as a demand driver or a reason for the project. Covers the 51 rows the first tag store left blank with a note, plus P8314 and P8323, and three tag leads from the discovery retries (P0246, P0225, P8195) (plan docs/plans/2026-10-16_us-gas-datacenter-subfloor.md).

values.DataCenterNotes: Summit Midstream's August 2026 release on the Double E expansion names data center development in Texas and New Mexico as a new source of demand for Double E, beyond the expansion capacity to Waha. No specific data center is named. Trade press repeats the same statement.

verifications.note: Summit Midstream release lists growth from data center developments in Texas and New Mexico for Double E.
Trade press repeats Summit's statement on data center demand for Double E.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Summit Midstream's August 2026 release says data center development in Texas and New Mexico is a demand growth opportunity for Double E. No campus is named. The pipeline press story repeats the same release.

values.DataCenterNotes: Williams' December 2025 fact sheet for Constitution cites data center and manufacturing construction as a reason the Northeast needs the pipeline. It says the Northeast got only 2 percent of national data center construction spending from 2020 to 2024. No specific data center is named.

verifications.note: Williams Constitution fact sheet lists lagging data center and manufacturing investment in the Northeast among the reasons for the pipeline.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The developer's own December 2025 Constitution fact sheet names data centers among the economic reasons for the pipeline. It is one of several drivers and no customer is named.

values.DataCenterNotes: In March 2024 EQT's chief executive said power demand from AI data centers in the southeastern market is something Mountain Valley Pipeline is set to serve. No specific data center is named.

verifications.note: Bloomberg story says EQT's chief executive tied Mountain Valley Pipeline to AI data center power demand in the Southeast.

resolutions.researcher_notes: A March 2024 Bloomberg story, run by Data Center Knowledge, quotes EQT's chief executive saying the pipeline will serve rising data center power demand in the Southeast. No campus is named.

values.DataCenterNotes: DT Midstream added a new 250 million cubic feet per day interconnect on the NEXUS mainline to supply a gas plant that powers a new data center in Ohio. The data center is not named.

verifications.note: DT Midstream first quarter 2026 earnings call, April 30, 2026: new NEXUS interconnect, 250 MMcf/d, supplies a behind-the-meter gas plant powering a new data center in Ohio.

resolutions.researcher_notes: On its earnings call of April 30, 2026, DT Midstream said it signed a new interconnect on NEXUS for 250 million cubic feet per day. It supplies the company's own gas plant that powers a new data center in Ohio. The company said it chose not to build a lateral, so the load sits on the NEXUS mainline. The data center is not named, so the tag is medium. The call transcript is from The Motley Fool. A second interconnect for another Ohio data center was reported later in 2026 but was not read here.

values.DataCenterNotes: Tallgrass's Cheyenne Power Hub in Laramie County, Wyoming, will burn gas from the Rockies Express Pipeline to power a data center campus known as Project Jade.

verifications.note: Power Engineering, May 2026: the hub's first-phase turbines are fueled by gas from Tallgrass' Rockies Express Pipeline; the hub serves the Project Jade data center.

resolutions.researcher_notes: A Power Engineering article from May 2026 says the first phase of Tallgrass's Cheyenne Power Hub will run on gas from the Rockies Express Pipeline. The hub serves a data center campus called Project Jade. No new lateral was reported, so this is demand on the existing line. One source was found; no second was searched because the session's web search budget ran out.

values.DataCenterNotes: A January 2026 Rextag industry blog names data centers, with utilities, industry and coal retirements, as demand drivers for gas pipeline expansion in Wisconsin, and names the Wisconsin Reliability Project as one of the expansions meeting that demand. It says Microsoft and Meta, among others, are looking at Wisconsin and Illinois for data center sites. No specific data center is tied to this pipeline.

verifications.note: Blog names the Wisconsin Reliability Project and says data centers, utility demand and coal retirements drive Midwest gas investment; names Microsoft and Meta targeting Wisconsin and Illinois.

resolutions.researcher_notes: A Rextag blog from January 2026 names data centers among the demand drivers for the Wisconsin Reliability Project. The project's own fact sheet and the energy agency table name utilities and coal-to-gas conversions only. The data center mention is regional and from a trade blog.

values.DataCenterNotes: A Williams blog post from August 2024 says the Southeast Supply Enhancement project is designed to provide reliable power where data center growth is expected, and points to Virginia as the largest data center hub. The federal regulator's certificate order in 2026 noted that Transco's market study cited data centers among the new large loads. No specific data center is named.

verifications.note: Williams blog: SSE is designed to provide reliable power where data center growth is expected; Virginia is the largest data center hub.
Reports that the federal regulator accepted a Transco market study citing data center load growth for the project.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Williams's August 2024 blog says the project is designed to supply power where data center growth is expected. A February 2026 law firm summary of the federal regulator's approval says Transco's market study cited data centers and manufacturing as large loads, and the regulator rejected a rival report that called data center demand speculative. No named campus.

values.DataCenterNotes: A January 2025 trade report on Kinder Morgan's Trident pipeline says the project is part of the growing AI data center trend in Texas, citing the chief executive's remarks in the fourth quarter 2024 earnings release. The pipeline's named contracts are for LNG and the Port Arthur industrial corridor. No specific data center is named.

verifications.note: Article reports Trident as part of the AI data center trend in Texas per CEO Kim Dang's Q4 2024 release remarks.

resolutions.researcher_notes: An Underground Infrastructure article from January 2025 reports that Kinder Morgan's chief executive tied Trident to Texas data center growth. The company's own project page names LNG and industrial demand only, so this is a weaker tie from press reporting of an earnings release.

values.DataCenterNotes: A January 2026 release from Intensity Infrastructure Partners and Rainbow Energy Center says the decision to advance Phase I of the 36-inch pipeline supports sustained data center growth, grid reliability and industrial development in North Dakota. Uncommitted capacity supports new gas-fired power along the route and at Coal Creek Station. No specific data center is named.

verifications.note: Release on advancing Phase I says the project supports sustained data center growth in North Dakota.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The developers' January 2026 release on advancing Phase I names data center growth among the reasons for the project. No campus or customer is named.
